reviewer: independent reviewer, fresh agent session with no builder context (AI review, not a human)
scope: Holistic source-locked architectural-clay review of the delivered texture-free v006 GLB, its 23 renders and 4 phone boards against the three locked references for calgary_15_connected_tower / brutalist_concrete_slab, treated as a new candidate; not a textured-keeper, runtime or engineering review.
decision_note: Zero P0 and zero P1. Seven P2 findings are open; three of the nine v005 findings are resolved, four are partly resolved and two are unresolved. Two declared limitations still need a person to accept them knowingly before activation: the near-flat street skyline, and the 9 m walkway stub with no support at its free end.

comparison_with_v005.overall: v006 is better than v005 on balance.
better: The clearance slits beside the walkway are closed.
The far corners no longer show the sky through two panes, and ribbon ends match ribbon middles in the elevations.
The parapet band is 3 px nearer the source and the reveal draws as a continuous line at distance.
The penthouse has eight panels to a face, as the source does.
No desk or light crosses the corner-room walls or the columns.
worse: The sunlit street-corner bay is lighter and flatter: three blind panes at luminance 68 in renders/match_front.png where v005 read 50 to 63 and the reference 30 to 42.
Three faint column bars (luminance about 100) show on the two lowest street-front ribbons where v005 had one, because the columns moved 0.2 m nearer the glass.
The walkway dark band is 2 to 3 px thinner in the street view, because the shaded soffit above the glass is shallower; the glass itself is not shorter.
The manifest roof contract now disagrees with the build (1.1 m parapet stated, 1.0 m built).
unchanged: Walkway glazed band height as seen

findings.title: The walkway glazed band is still short; moving the glass forward did not change what shows
evidence: GLB: the walkway glass is now at z 11.12 and 6.88, 0.11 m behind the tube faces at 11.23 and 6.77 (v005: 0.25 m). The opening is unchanged: y 9.75 to 11.95 (2.20 m), glass 9.82 to 11.88 (2.06 m), crown 1.15 m and belly 1.25 m of a 4.60 m tube.

Fitted street view, dark band from head to sill at the same pixel columns. x=860: reference rows 350 to 411 (61 px); v006 rows 366 to 416 (50 px); v005 rows 364 to 417 (53 px). x=920: reference 341 to 405 (64 px); v006 358 to 410 (52 px); v005 356 to 411 (55 px). The 2 to 3 px lost since v005 are the shaded soffit above the glass, which is now shallower; the glass itself shows as before.
boards/phone-street.png lower image about x 780 to 1025, y 1315 to 1440.
findings.why_it_matters: The visible glazed band is about 40 percent of the tube against 47 to 48 percent in both sources, so the walkway still reads a little heavy in the belly. From the street the camera looks up at about nine degrees, so a sill ledge 0.14 m shallower uncovers less than a pixel of glass; the head and sill have to move for the band to grow.
findings.suggested_correction: Raise the opening to about 2.45 m, for example sill at 9.65 m and head at 12.10 m (crown about 1.0 m, belly about 1.15 m), and re-measure at x = 860 and 920 in the street view and x = 850 to 1000 in the oblique.

findings.why_it_matters: The top band is nearer the source than in v005 but is still the fattest of the five, and the top ribbon head is still 11 px low. The manifest and the build now disagree about the parapet height.
findings.suggested_correction: Take a further 0.10 to 0.15 m off the parapet (top band about 1.92 m), refit the street camera so the ribbon heads land near rows 116, 224, 333 and 440 at x=640, and correct roof_contract.

findings.title: Corner blinds read as flat panels three panes wide, and one sightline per storey still crosses the building
evidence: GLB: 32 blinds, each a 20 mm plane 0.13 m behind the glass and 4.07 m long, on both glazed sides of every corner room on the four office storeys. They cover 18 percent of each street-front ribbon and 20 percent of each flank ribbon. Corner rooms are 4.1 m square inside (walls at 4.5 m from each face).

renders/match_front.png, second ribbon from the top on the street front: the blind panes average luminance 68 (x 560 to 580 and x 622 to 643) against 44 for the panes beside them (x 450 to 520). The reference reads 30 and 42 at the same two panes and 37 mid-ribbon; v005 read 50 and 63.
Elevations: ribbon ends and middles are now within 8 levels of each other in renders/front.png, rear.png, left_side.png and right_side.png (v005: ends 11 to 16 lighter).

Background seen through the office storeys has fallen sharply: renders/front_corner.png 3,729 to 414 px, rear_ground.png 3,367 to 250 px, west_ground.png 4,217 to 232 px, bridge_contact.png 6,655 to 426 px.

What remains: a passage 2 m square beside each corner of the core (x 16 to 18, z 13.75 to 15.75 and its mirrors) lets a straight line cross from one glazed side to the next touching only glass; 303 to 377 of 8,820 sampled rays per passage do so on the second and third storeys. It shows as a bright rectangle in renders/front_corner.png x 336 to 346, y 699 to 715 and x 1189 to 1198, y 702 to 713; rear_ground.png x 1031 to 1036, y 618 to 627; match_front.png x 830 to 837, y 522 to 527; and bridge_junction.png x 1042 to 1071, y 992 to 1062.

Perimeter columns now stand 0.9 m behind the glass (v005 1.1 m). renders/match_front.png shows faint bars of luminance about 100 at x 216 to 219, 331 to 336 and 475 to 482 on the two lowest ribbons; v005 had one, at x 478 to 485.
findings.why_it_matters: The far corners no longer show the sky, which was the defect. In exchange the sunlit street corner now carries a flat block lighter than the rest of the ribbon where the source is dark, and the corner rooms show no depth. The remaining see-through patch is small but reads as a lit doorway in a dark storey.
findings.suggested_correction: Put the blinds in a darker role or set them 0.4 to 0.5 m back so the band shades them, limit them to two panes each side, and stagger the passage walls or add a screen so no straight line crosses the building.

findings.title: Thin offsets and fine joints still alias
evidence: Unchanged, as the builder says: granite and penthouse panels stand 11 to 31 mm proud and panel joints are 12 to 30 mm across.
renders/aerial.png east ground storey about x 990 to 1290, y 720 to 940: granite joints break into dots.
renders/right_side.png penthouse about x 754 and x 865, y 315 to 378: faint extra seams where the upper-tier panels are split at the louvre and beside it.

GLB: at every joint between band panels the joint strip stops 20 mm short of the top and bottom of the band, leaving a notch 30 mm wide and 20 mm tall that opens to the room behind (ray test at z 11.235 to 11.265, y 11.95 to 11.97). It is far below the size of a pixel in every render.
GLB: the end caps of the sixteen first-band panels still have a vertex on an edge without a matching split. They are hidden inside the joints.
One strand is better as a side effect of the taller reveal: see V6-P2-03.
findings.why_it_matters: None of this is an error in a still. These are the lines that crawl and shimmer once the camera moves in the runtime, whichever renderer draws them.
findings.suggested_correction: Use offsets of at least 20 to 30 mm and wider joints, and run the joint strips the full height of the band.

findings.suggested_correction: List the eight fitted points with their residuals and declare the west-end residual, or refit with the south-west pier foot included.

findings.title: Some ceiling lights still run into the core face and the shop party walls

street_view: Five storeys: a taller recessed ground storey and four ribbon storeys under a flat parapet, seen from the front-right corner.
All five concrete bands read as nearly the same height (48 to 52 px at the corner); each has a projecting cap strip over a bold dark line 8 px tall.
A board-formed penthouse stands 58 to 63 px above the parapet over the left-centre of the front.

Dark bronze ribbon glazing with close mullions wraps the corner with a bronze corner post. The corner panes are as dark as the rest (luminance 30 to 42); the last front pane is a warmer brown. The left third of the front and the flank reflect the sky.
Front ground storey: five bays between six square aggregate piers, storefront glazing with a transom, one pair of doors in the second bay from the corner, timber panelling in the corner bay.
Flank ground storey: a short glazed return, blank aggregate panels between piers, a dark service door at the far end.
The walkway leaves the flank at the third storey as a grey concrete tube with rounded edges and a glazed band 61 to 64 px tall, a little under half its depth. It runs out of frame.
oblique: The same five storeys with ribbons on both visible sides and band joints at the structural lines; a continuous dark line under every cap strip.
The walkway joins about a third of the way back along the flank, has a flat roof with eased edges over glazing 44 to 46 px tall, and lands on a brick neighbour; a flank pier stands beneath it.
Flat gravel roof inside a concrete parapet with a dark flashing line.

A centred penthouse in two tiers of panels with tie holes, eight panels across each visible face, with a door and a large louvre on the flank-facing side and an open well in its rear right corner. A skylight dome sits on the roof in front of it.
roof_plan: Footprint about 670 by 613 px with the street front along the bottom edge.
A well in the rear right corner of the penthouse holding one square unit.
The walkway is about 68 px wide on the right flank, centred about 28 percent of the depth back from the front, and runs to a neighbour.
A hatch in front of the penthouse, a small vent to its right, a box and two conduit runs on its roof.

positive_observations: Model hash, byte count and source hashes match the build report and manifest; the GLB carries no images or textures; the boards carry the model hash prefix.
Massing, storey count, bay count, piers, entrance bay, walkway level and position agree with the sources; the fitted roof plan registers closely.
The walkway mouth is solid on both sides with no slit, and the tube is flat-topped with smooth eased edges.
The ribbons read as continuous dark strips on all four sides; ribbon heights match both perspective sources within a few pixels.
All four sides and the roof are complete in the same band and ribbon grammar; openings are real wall sections with recessed frames, glass and something behind.
Every pier stands on a plinth and carries the first band through a bearing pad; no component is isolated; lowest geometry is at grade; the roof is fully covered seen from above.
Every triangle is wound consistently with its normal.
The ground storey is unchanged from v005; renders/entrance_contact.png is pixel-identical at a tolerance of 24 levels.
Whole-building views include grade, the full footprint and the highest point with neutral margin.
limitations: Stills only. Flicker, depth precision and crawling lines in a moving runtime camera were not observed.
Runtime placement, terrain fit, entrance routing and saved reload were not tested.
The generator and renderer were neither read nor run, so "rebuilds to the same bytes" is not verified and I cannot say how much of the pale reveal shading is the review renderer.
The fitted camera parameters and the points used for fitting were not available; registration was judged by overlay and pixel profiles.
The references carry no scale and disagree with each other in places; the 45 m width rests on the manifest assumption of a 3.9 m storey.
Interiors were seen only through the glazing; there are no interior cameras.

Faint short tick marks on the cap strips beside some joints (for example renders/right_side.png about x 831, y 513 to 528) still have no geometry behind them in the GLB. I could not identify their cause; they look like a renderer artefact.
